proposed.explanation: Both EFID and COMI show strong one-year profit growth (EFID net profit up ~68% to 2.70 billion EGP; COMI net profit up ~49% to 82.26 billion EGP), and EPS has risen for both. However, the evidence provided is limited to a single year of consolidated profit and EPS figures. For an investor whose stated goal is to lower risk before retirement, with a 3-year horizon, low willingness to accept losses, and low financial ability to withstand losses, the following critical information is missing to make a responsible recommendation: (1) multi-year earnings and revenue trends to judge sustainability; (2) balance-sheet data (debt, liquidity, leverage) to assess financial risk; (3) dividend history and policy, which matters for an income-oriented retiree; (4) valuation metrics (P/E, P/B) to judge whether current prices are reasonable; (5) sector/industry risk and business-model details; (6) any risk factors, going-concern notes, or regulatory issues. Without these, I cannot determine whether holding, reducing, or adding to either position is appropriate for a low-risk profile. The positive profit growth is encouraging but does not, by itself, justify a buy or a sell for a risk-averse investor. I recommend seeking the full annual reports (balance sheets, cash-flow statements, risk disclosures) and, if possible, a second year of data before acting. In the meantime, the investor's existing positions (600 EFID at 20.40 EGP = 12,240 EGP; 150 COMI at 128 EGP = 19,200 EGP; 5,000 EGP cash; total ≈ 36,440 EGP) can be left unchanged pending further information, but no new purchase or sale is warranted on the evidence at hand.

limitations: Only one fiscal year of comparison (FY2025 vs FY2024) is available; no multi-year trend.
No balance-sheet, cash-flow, or debt information for either company.
No dividend data, which is critical for a retiree seeking income and lower risk.
No valuation metrics (P/E, P/B, dividend yield) to assess whether current prices are attractive or overvalued.
No sector, business-model, or risk-factor disclosures.

COMI EPS unit line reads 'EGP thousands' (a table-wide unit); the per-share figures (18.25, 14.72) are interpreted as EGP per share, which is the standard convention, but this should be confirmed in the full report.
